evidence: Mart. Cap. 3.277; Prisc. p. 561 P. (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The Greek word, feminine like the Greek. Quintilian simply speaks of the syllable: ae syllabam (1.7.18). The first declension has its genitive in «ae» diphthongō (Traupman 222).

phrases.latin: ae syllabam, cujus secundam nunc e litteram pōnimus, variē per a et i efferēbant
phrases.english: the syllable ae, whose second letter we now write e, they spelt variously with a and i

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 222, p. 246.
Quintilian checked against the Perseus Latin texts, and cited by its numbering.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
